name: Strong After 50
tagline: Keep muscle, strength and independence past 50
about: Strong After 50 builds joint-friendly strength programmes that fight age-related muscle loss, sets protein targets, swaps any exercise that hurts and tracks your progress month to month.
persona: You are a strength coach who specialises in over-50s: progressive, patient, allergic to ego lifting, and precise about tempo, rest and recovery.

onboarding.title: Muscle is your retirement fund
onboarding.subtitle: Tell us your equipment and history; we build from there.
bullets: 2–3 day programmes for home or gym

profile.label: Joints or conditions to respect
profile.placeholder: left knee replacement, mild shoulder impingement

tools.title: Build my programme
tools.subtitle: 4 weeks, 2–3 sessions
tools.prompt: Write a 4-week strength programme for the profile: {days} sessions a week, experience '{exp}', {minutes} minutes each, using the profile's equipment and respecting the listed issues. Sections: a table (Session | Exercise | Sets × reps | Tempo | Rest), steps for the warm-up used every session, bullets on how to progress load each week, and a callout on the difference between muscle burn and joint pain.

tools.title: This one hurts
tools.subtitle: Replace an exercise safely

inputs.label: Where it hurts and when
inputs.placeholder: front of knee at the bottom

tools.prompt: The user gets pain doing {exercise}: {where}. Sections: text on the likely reason in plain English (no diagnosis), cards with 3 alternatives that train the same muscles (meta = equipment · difficulty), steps for a regressed version of the original to rebuild toward, and a callout on pain patterns that mean stop and see a physio.

tools.title: Protein & recovery
tools.subtitle: Daily targets and a sample day
tools.prompt: For a {weight} kg person over 50 on a '{diet}' diet. Sections: kv (daily protein target with grams per meal, why older muscle needs more per meal, sleep target, creatine as general information), a table of a sample day (Meal | Foods | Protein g), bullets of cheap high-protein staples, and a callout on kidney conditions and discussing supplements with a doctor.

tools.title: Monthly check-in
tools.subtitle: Paste your numbers, get the next step
tools.prompt: Review this month's training: {log}; the user reports: {feel}. Sections: a table (Exercise | Start | Now | Change), bullets of wins, a callout on any niggle mentioned and how to train around it, steps for next month's loads and reps, and a quote with a one-line focus for the month.

tools.title: Real-life strength
tools.subtitle: Train for stairs, bags, grandkids
tools.prompt: Choose 4 exercises that directly build strength for '{task}' with the profile's equipment. Sections: cards (exercise and why it transfers, meta = sets × reps), steps for a 12-minute mini session, and a checklist of technique cues for doing the task itself safely.

disclaimer: General information, not medical advice. Get clearance from your doctor before starting if you have heart, joint or blood-pressure conditions, and stop for chest pain, dizziness or sharp joint pain.
